name: inprocess-obi-apb-two-ip-timer-i2c-f1f6
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU reaches two independent APB3 MMIO targets by address: the PULP timer with an F5 IRQ declaration and the PULP I2C held at idle pins, plus an optional ZipDMA control window.
notes: One OBI CPU (Ibex RVFI) reaches two independent APB3 MMIO targets by address instead of one CPU x IP wiring: target 0 is the PULP timer at 0x40001000, target 1 is the PULP I2C at 0x40002000, and the optional ZipDMA control window is at 0x40003000 inside the fixed RAM image 0x10000..0x30000.

Both target windows are the profiles' own 4 KiB APB windows. Both bases are 4 KiB-aligned, the windows touch at 0x40002000/0x40003000 without overlapping, and neither overlaps RAM or the 16-byte DMA control window. The timer registers are TIMER0_COUNT(0), TIMER0_CTRL(4) and TIMER0_CMP(8); the I2C registers are PRESCALER(0), CTRL(4), RX(8), STATUS(12), TX(16) and CMD(20).

Only target 0 declares F5 facts, through configs/behaviors/pulp_timer_f5.json: irq_o[0], a 16-tick pulse, trigger writes [[4,0],[8,0],[0,4294967295]] and the TIMER0_COUNT status word at offset 0. The PULP I2C profile declares interrupts: [] and records interrupt_o as observe-only, so it can be reached by address but cannot be a second F5 IRQ source.

The CPU has one IRQ line and the F5 ISR has one status/result/clear cell set. If a later declaration gave both targets complete F5 facts, myfuzz.composition.multi_target.target_for_f5 would refuse it as unsupported-f5:multiple-target-irq-sources; that refusal is the honest limit, not an address-routing conflict.

The I2C pad inputs scl_pad_i and sda_pad_i are held at 1 (open-drain idle) in both fixed_inputs and tuning.fixed_inputs; the generic target template owns every other non-bus input. The duplication is intentional: the target request builder reads tuning and the generated header reads fixed_inputs, so the two declarations must agree.

The targets list is consumed by myfuzz.composition.multi_target; the current single-target entry and C++ host still read source_profile/target_window, so this file is a declaration for the integration and not evidence of a real RTL or Verilator run. No such run is claimed here.
